why: A moved more traffic and proved it (37 live requests, a real bypass fixed in ChatAnthropic's clientOptions, and the presence_penalty field that was silently keeping every Custom-provider request off Router), then did the CTO work the bar asks for: per-feature labels, a policy that splits tier by who is waiting (Flex for unattended batch at a measured -50%, standard pinned for keystroke paths), and a ranked set of proposals with measured prices — the best of them rethinking whether the hot call should exist in its current form at all. B's migration is competent and its honesty about retired model defaults is good, but its system judgment is one settings field plus a blanket service_tier=default — it missed that Anthropic's SDK never saw the plugin's fetch, missed the presence_penalty blocker, flattened its own batch feature onto the interactive tier, and left model choice, caching, spend caps, shadow models and the n=5 auto-suggest call unexamined.
A_best: It found and fixed the two invisible blockers — ChatAnthropic reading clientOptions rather than configuration, and the shipped presence_penalty 0.5 in the Custom body template — each verified live, which is what actually makes the move cover Anthropic and Custom users rather than only OpenAI Chat; and the auto-suggest proposal (one json_schema call on gpt-4.1-nano at $0.00003 vs ~$0.00115 for n=5 on gpt-4o) is the right call to question, correctly priced, and simultaneously makes the plugin's highest-frequency request routable.
B_best: The d1 needs-decision is sharply framed and correct: four of the five shipped model defaults are not Router catalog ids, model_map could silently answer with a different model, and in a plugin whose whole settings tab is model choice that is a product call, not an engineering one — it refused to quietly change what the user picked.
A_worst: Its m1 claim that the three raw-HTTP Custom sites are covered sits directly against the validator's not_routing for exactly those sites, and seven of twelve routed sites are unverified — the live probes and the scanner disagree, and A argues the scanner is wrong rather than closing the gap; passing the same object as both configuration and clientOptions across all thirteen LangChain classes is also a broader behaviour change than 'inert' admits.
B_worst: The system-level judgment barely exists for this product: one global service_tier=default sweeps away Flex on the batch runs B itself labels 'batch-generate' (nobody is waiting on a folder sweep), caching was dismissed on a token-minimum argument without measuring a real rendered template, and the n=5 auto-suggest call — the plugin's hottest path and one Router cannot serve at all — is never noticed, let alone reconsidered.
